messages.author: 8bb91f4cbf7e32b6
messages.subject: Latent Mean Estimation
parts:
Hi everybody. 
I'm writing here to clarify whether and how Lavaan allows estimating latent variable means. Surfing the WEB (https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/280829/how-to-compute-and-interpret-the-mean-of-a-latent-variable-in-structural-equatio )  I have found this strategy, that proved to be wrong though:

library(lavaan) 
data = data("HolzingerSwineford1939") 
HS.model = 
    "visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 
     textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6 
     speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 

 x1 ~ 0*1 # Setting the intercepts of the manifest variables to zero
 x4 ~ 0*1 
 x7 ~ 0*1 
 visual ~ 1 # Estimating latent means freely                  
 textual ~ 1 
 speed ~ 1 # 

" fit = sem(HS.model, 
                  data=HolzingerSwineford1939, 
                  meanstructure =TRUE) 


Here the user constrains three intercepts of the observed variables to zero (i.e., x1, x4, x7), and then estimate the latent variable intercepts (i.e., visual, textual, and speed). Although the solution seems working, a closer look to the estimated latent variable intercepts (i.e., visual, textual, and speed) reveals that the estimated values are exactly the intercepts for the three indicators now set to zero (i.e., x1, x4, x7), and not the latent mean. 

My question is: Is it possible to estimate latent variable means using Lavaan. 
If so, which is the correct method? 

Thanks in advance

Emanuele

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Latent Mean Estimation
parts:
Hi, Emanuele.

You actually did estimate latent means, but the way you scaled them gave you answers you didn't expect. Like latent variances, latent means are arbitrary and need to be scaled. The usual way to use latent means is when you have a multiple-group analysis--otherwise, the mean structure is usually unconstrained incidental parameters.

In any case, have you looked at this page of the lavaan tutorial? https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/means.html It shows mean-structures with the H-S data.

What question are you trying to answer with the means?

Pat

messages.subject: Re: Latent Mean Estimation
parts:
Hi Pat, thanks for your answer. Ok, I see what you mean: There is no way to "get the "true" latent mean, no matter what, I will always get an arbitrary number derived from the scaling system employed, right?
Not only I would like to apply constrains and check for mean differences, but also get a descriptive information on the exact (latent) mean level for the subsamples (e.g., on a scale to 1 to 5, group A has a latent mean of 2.34, whereas group B has a latent mean of 3.21). Do you think that scaling the latent mean on the indicator with the highest factor loading would (at least) bring me close to my ideal true value? 
Best,

Emanuele

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Latent Mean Estimation
parts:
Emanuele,

No, the loading doesn't have anything to do with it.

The most common method for multiple-group comparisons in my experience is to constrain the intercepts (and loadings) to equality across groups, which puts the latent means on the same metric across groups. Then you set one of the groups to have a latent mean of zero to fix the location. The other group means will be relative to that group.

Pat

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Latent Mean Estimation
parts:
Emanuele

You can use the measEq.syntax function from semTools to create the syntax from these model for you.
In any case the "actual" mean will be arbitrary and not very meaningful by itself. If you do the meultiple groups apporach the group means will be meaningful in cmparison to each other


## The famous Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3

speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

?measEq.syntax

eq_syn <- measEq.syntax(HS.model, ID.fac = "std.lv",
                          meanstructure=T,
                          group.equal = c("loadings","intercepts"),
                          group="school", data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
cat(as.character( eq_syn ))
summary( eq_syn )

fit <- cfa(as.character( eq_syn ),
           data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
           meanstructure=T, group = "school")
summary(fit)
